text:
sophie: alert from synthetics — spike in 502/503s hitting /prompt-proxy at ~12:03 UTC, canary pool memory surge. paging oncall.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered for oncall-lee (P1) — Incident INC-2026-054 created. Auto-notes: increased error rate, affected route: /v1/prompt-proxy
oncall-lee: picking this up. seeing repeated OOMs on canary pods. linking logs.
raj: confirmed in k8s: pods prompt-proxy-canary-{5,7,9} OOMKilled. CPU fine, heap creeping. might be a dependency leak in the new image.
liam: are we still routing a slice of prod traffic to the canary? what %?
anna: 5% via feature flag `prompt_proxy_switch` set to canary for experiments. deadman trigger should auto-cut at 3% errors for 2m but it hasn't tripped — looks like metric reporting lag.
megan: customer reports: some requests returning 502s, subset of endpoints; support queue getting DMs. severity > P1 for some enterprise customers.
support-bot: creating incident runbook link: https://internal.redwood/INC-2026-054
sophie: posting logs from node:
```
kubelet: OOMKilled container prompt-proxy-canary-7f9
heap snapshot: 97% used
stacktrace: n/a (short lived)
```
oncall-lee: quick triage: reduce exposure first. recommend immediate kill-switch of feature flag and fallback traffic to stable route. pinging infra for proxy swap if needed.
raj: agree. flipping `prompt_proxy_switch` to stable now (console + API).
raj: `curl -X POST "https://console.internal/api/flags/prompt_proxy_switch" -d '{"state":"stable"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ***"`
raj: done — flag set to stable. verifying traffic.
liam: seeing traffic move off canary within 30s, error rate dropping in metrics.
anna: metrics: 5xx rate on /v1/prompt-proxy dropped from 6.8% -> 0.8% in 90s. latency back to baseline.
megan: support: acknowledging impacted customers, sending templates, and tracking for credits. tentative list of affected account IDs added to the ticket.
oncall-lee: good. but the canary pods still crash when they spin. need to prevent accidental re-rolls. tagging image as bad and removing canary pool from autoscaler pools.
raj: pinned: `promt-proxy:v2026-03-15-canary` marked unsafe. also created a short-lived admission rule to block that image in canary namespace.
incident-bot: runbook step executed: feature flag kill-switch manual flip recorded (actor: raj). automatic deadman not used due to metrics lag. All changes logged.
liam: question: did rollback of canary require db change? i think no — only proxy layer.
anna: confirmed no DB migration. safe to re-deploy once root cause fixed.
sophie: thinking root cause is regression in third-party lib that expands internal cache under certain payload shapes. will instrument heap snapshots on the next candidate and run local fuzz tests.
megan: ETA for communications update? we pushed initial ack to customers, will send incident follow-up in 60-90m once we have scope.
support-bot: adding affected customers to spreadsheet and tagging CSMs.
oncall-lee: handing off resiliency verification to raj for next 60m, i'll stay on standby for escalation. @raj — take the lead, update this thread with status and mitigation timeline.
raj: taking over. next steps: collect heap dumps, run canary in isolated env, test with payloads mirroring production. will coordinate with SRE for a safe re-roll window.
liam: long term: add a proactive canary memwatcher + faster deadman on metrics ingestion for that route.
anna: +1. also need a faster control-plane flag path (lower eventual consistency) for emergency flips.
megan: support will prepare postmortem note draft and customer impact summary.
oncall-lee: nice work. closing the active alert window for now — systems stable on stable route. will keep incident open for follow-up actions and RCA.
sophie: thanks all — please add any follow-up tasks to INC-2026-054 and assign owners. cc: #postmortems for scheduling.
raj: updated ticket with immediate mitigations and owners. will attach heap dumps and reproducer steps.
megan: scheduling a 30m post-incident sync at 15:30 UTC. invite sent.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-054 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Handoff: raj (owner) for 60m, then follow-up doc owner: megan.
oncall-lee: handing off to next shift. if anything spikes, page me and i'll re-join. :thumbsup:
megan: noted. adding timeline + customer impact to follow-up doc. :memo:
